sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Cospower’s FY26 sales nearly quadrupled, but receivables rose ₹30.31 crore and reported operating cash was negative ₹15.30 crore. Restricted-bank and historical cash-definition adjustments are kept separate rather than mistaken for missing cash. Its tested power-quality products and capacity expansion offer a runway; funding, order repeatability and very coarse trading lots require careful valuation. Full applicable review is completed with quality scores, conditional funded scenarios and expected-return and tradability IAS gaps. Strong operating growth does not yet establish strong cash compounding, particularly at the dated secondary valuation.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of20 October2026; BSE SME543172, Cospower Engineering, ISIN INE0CQB01010. Standalone Indian AS,₹crore unless indicated. Five-year model,15% nominal hurdle and₹5lakh reference. October19 secondary₹2,950 close is dated, not live. Issued1,836,500 shares are confirmed by annual capital and September AGM voting. Audit gates are distinct: no established integrity or financeability failure, but complete tradability evidence is missing.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: All nine quality factors are individually supported. REV 8 reflects a 54.7% five-year CAGR with a one-point repeatability adjustment; CASH 4 reflects negative recent conversion without imposing a persistent cap from one year. R remains NS: the conditional financed base IRR would map to 1 against a 15% hurdle, but the project budget, FD availability, bank headroom and order repeatability are not sufficiently verified for an expected-return score. D 3 and P 3 are valuation-risk judgments. L remains NS because eight calendar/provider gaps are unresolved. IAS bounds retain missing weights without renormalisation; supported quality scores are not suppressed.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Cospower supplies reactive-power compensation, harmonic filters, capacitors and engineered power-quality systems. The founders trace operating experience to2004, while listed corporate identity is the2010 entity. Engineering, type testing, customization and installation serve industrial/grid customers. Damping resistors were introduced and supplied to solar installations during FY26. BESS, SVG and transformers are strategic possibilities, not booked standalone segments or contracted incremental revenue.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Customer qualification, testing and specialized power-quality design create moderate barriers. Shreem Electric is a useful product comparator: its October2025 rating describes moderate entry barriers, tender competition and advantages from operating history/certification. Shreem FY25income₹354.47crore,11.73% EBITDA margin and245-day cash cycle show that technical products can still carry weak cash economics. Hitachi Energy India FY26sales₹8,147.7crore illustrate far greater grid-system scale, but HVDC/transformer/service mix makes its valuation an unsuitable direct benchmark. No mechanical peer P/E is imported.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Operating sales FY21–26 were₹12.0974/12.0957/14.0712/22.2927/27.7013/107.1733crore. These are operating revenue, not directors’ occasionally mislabeled total-income figures. Five-year CAGR is54.7%; the latest year’s near-fourfold jump dominates the trend. FY26PAT₹13.0222crore versus₹1.5328crore reflects scale and operating leverage, but receivables grew₹30.3149crore. A full customer/order concentration bridge was not available in the reports reviewed; repeatability cannot be inferred from one large execution year.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Management targets FY27revenue above₹150crore and a new80,000sqft Virar plant on more than two acres with claimed near-fivefold capacity and150kV testing. Damping-resistor capacity is targeted to double byMarch2027. The annual message’s prospective commissioning date “Q4FY26” conflicts with its publication chronology, so completion timing remains unverified rather than assumed already operational. New product testing and actual supplies support progress; project budget, utilization and collections must substantiate returns on the₹16.038crore equity raise.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Four directors received aggregate₹1.674crore versus₹0.7482crore. September29 AGM approved revised annual remuneration of₹0.6625crore each for two executives, including minimum-pay provisions in inadequate-profit periods; interested promoters did not vote those special resolutions. Related finance leadership merits independent oversight. The note labeled “loan given to related party” conflicts with borrowings presentation; the same₹0.1014crore is treated as director funding liability, not asserted as a loan out. Auditor tenure ended and a new firm was appointed in2025; no resignation-driven adverse inference is made. Disclosure of no litigation/fraud is limited to the auditor’s stated scope, not universal assurance.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26CFO−₹15.3034crore is driven by₹30.3149crore receivables,₹4.6970crore payable reduction and advances, partly offset by₹7.7597crore inventory release. Reported CFO less₹3.1371crore fixed purchases is−₹18.4405crore before strategic investing. Restricted-bank balances grew₹3.5380crore inside operating asset movements: reclassifying that amount to investing yields CFO−₹11.7654crore and equal CFI reduction, with no net cash change. Capital advances and tax/accrual details still prevent exact normalized FCF. FY25original closing cash₹8.7940 versus comparative₹7.8881 differs by₹0.9059crore margin FD; CFO/CFI changes reconcile to this within rounding, not missing cash. Current receivables₹41.5565crore include₹7.7120crore older than six months and₹1.8777crore older than a year. Cash₹1.8524, currentFD₹10.3051, recurring deposit₹0.4024 and pledged margins₹4.4439 are separately tracked against₹27.6880crore face debt; current maturities are not added twice.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Model correction — 20 October 2026: The opening-claim treatment in our earlier scenario calculations was incomplete. This revision explicitly bridges identified current settlements, retained net noncurrent claims and uncertain-composition sensitivities. The updated model replaces the earlier scenario version; the companies’ historical financial figures and published accounts have not changed.

Dated secondary close₹2,950 implies₹541.77crore market cap and41.6×static earnings using current shares, not weightedEPS. Bear/base/bull cases grow sales5%/20%/32%, use14%/19%/23% EBITDA margins,48%/38%/30%NWC, projectcapex₹20/20/30crore plus3%maintenance, and8×/12×/16×exitEBITDA. All annual borrowing, repayment, interest, tax and cash-floor effects are linked. Conditional bear/base/bull terminal prices are ₹706.30/₹3365.17/₹8921.79, with annual returns -24.87%/2.67%/24.77%. The base 15% hurdle entry is ₹1673.09. These are conditional estimates, not actionable targets. Capex₹10/20/40crore, FD availability, dilution, two-way growth/multiple, hurdle and trading-cost tests are saved. New draws incur half-year interest, with ordinary repayments at year-end; tax, interest and borrowing are solved jointly. The opening-claim bridge pays ₹2.522700 crore of identified opening income-tax provision and ₹0.776000 crore of excluded current employee/expense/interest provisions once in FY27, separately from tax and operating costs on forecast profit. It also deducts ₹0.183650 crore for the approved post-March dividend as financing cash outflow; an October buyer receives no modeled entitlement to that earlier record-date dividend. A further ₹0.225500 crore of net noncurrent employee/deposit claims is deducted from terminal equity, not forced into immediate cash payment. Future compensation and operating costs are cash funded in the model, with the opening net deficit held constant rather than invented annual deficit growth. Normal statutory, salary, expense and interest dues already in opening working capital are not charged twice.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: A few large projects may not repeat, while receivables remain unpaid and new plant absorbs capital. Weak collections force more bank funding, reducing interest cover and potentially requiring dilutive equity. A10% receivable loss is₹4.16crore before tax, roughly32%ofFY26PAT. Severe scenario combines shrinking sales,8%margin,55%NWC, unavailableFD,₹5crore extra cash use and5×exit multiple. A viable engineering company can still produce permanent investor loss from a high entry multiple and poor exit liquidity. Impairment risk: High. Under that severe case, peak required debt is ₹64.74 crore and terminal common equity remains zero. This requirement is not a sanctioned credit facility. With the opening-claim convention, the severe case requires peak modeled debt of ₹64.7384 crore, terminal price ₹0.0000 and annual return -100.0000%. These are conditional funding requirements, not evidence of committed facilities.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At unchanged shares,5×/10× price needs₹2709/₹5418crore owner equity value. At20×terminalP/E and12%net margin this implies₹1129/₹2257crore annual sales, versus₹107.17crore now. Even a5×capacity claim does not establish that revenue, utilization, margin or cash conversion. Further capacity and working capital would need funding; more shares increase required enterprise scale. Five-year5×/10× is speculative, not supported by the funded base case.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Require customer-wise collection progress and orders rather than just revenue targets. Track >six-month debtors against₹7.71crore, receivables/sales, collateral additions and supplier advances. Confirm Virar commissioning date, nameplate by product, approved project budget and incremental utilization. Verify current FD restrictions and unused bank facilities before relying on financing assumptions. Monitor executive pay relative to cash generated. Obtain complete BSE daily calendar/history and live lot/circuit/depth data: one125-share lot costs₹368,750 and two exceed the₹5lakh reference.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed applicable review supports a technically credible growth business with weak recent cash conversion and demanding valuation. Quality scores and conditional financed scenarios are retained, but R is NS rather than a scored expected return. IAS is not ranked because expected-return inputs and full tradability remain unverified. No purchase or allocation is recommended. The thesis strengthens only if collections and productive expansion catch up with reported profit and price offers sufficient margin for execution and liquidity risk.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Four original annual reports support six years of operating revenue and historical cash analysis; the FY21 report uses rupees rather than lakhs. Original September AGM results verify share count and pay approvals. Shreem rating and Hitachi primary release provide limited economic comparison, not complete peer dossiers. Secondary history has52 observations in a60-session reference window: observed-only5%exit6.87days and conditional zero-gap10.34days are sensitivity bounds, not fabricated no-trade evidence. Current funding, customer concentration and capacity commissioning remain material model uncertainties. The opening-claim reconciliation distinguishes current cash settlements, normal operating liabilities already in working capital, net noncurrent employee/deposit claims retained at exit, and uncertain composition bounds. March balances are not asserted to remain outstanding in October. No immediate payment of all noncurrent provisions is assumed.

valuation.units: INR crore except shares and rupees per share
valuation.horizon: Five annual steps from FY26 reference; not a verified October balance sheet
valuation.funding_note: March equity raise is already in assets; no second addition of₹16.038 crore. Current FD is treated only as a project funding reserve, with unavailable sensitivity. Current maturities are included in debt. No new capital is assumed committed. No future dividend entitlement assumed from the FY26₹1 dividend whose record date preceded the dated quote.
valuation.formulas: EBITDA=sales×margin; tax=max(0,(EBITDA−2%sales−interest)×26%); FCF=EBITDA−interest−tax−deltaNWC−projectcapex−3%sales maintenance. Release projectFD against projectcapex only, exclude unspent terminalFD. Borrow to₹2crore cash floor, then repay excess cash. Equity=max(0,terminalEBITDA×multiple−debt+cash); price=equity×1e7/shares; five-yearIRR=(price/2950)^0.2−1; entry=price/1.15^5. New borrowing incurs half-year interest in the year drawn. Ordinary excess-cash repayments occur at year-end and receive no same-year interest saving. Curis collateral-funded FD overdraft repayment retains its explicit half-year timing. Interest, positive-profit cash tax and funding draw are solved jointly to a 1e-12 crore tolerance; new borrowing is a funding requirement, not a committed facility. Opening-claim extension: first-year operating cash deducts identified excluded current tax/employee/expense claims once. Approved post-anchor dividends are separate financing cash outflows, with no buyer entitlement added. Terminal equity=max(0,original operating enterprise/equity bridge before its zero floor - retained net noncurrent claim). Normal WC liabilities are already captured and are not charged twice. The full-current-provision bound, where shown, replaces the unresolved zero-settlement reference rather than adding another copy of that liability.
valuation.capacity_and_cost_limits: All demand cases stay below5×FY26 sales, but the claimed5×plant capacity has no verified product-specific nameplate/commissioning bridge. Project₹20–30crore and sensitivities₹10–40crore are analyst assumptions, not approved full budgets. No BESS/transformer acquisition earnings are added. Current tax and margin normalization reflect the mix and funding uncertainty rather than mechanically repeating FY26PAT growth.
valuation.interest_timing_convention: New borrowing incurs half-year interest in the year drawn. Ordinary excess-cash repayments occur at year-end and receive no same-year interest saving. Curis collateral-funded FD overdraft repayment retains its explicit half-year timing. Interest, positive-profit cash tax and funding draw are solved jointly to a 1e-12 crore tolerance; new borrowing is a funding requirement, not a committed facility.
valuation.opening_claim_convention: Known current exclusions paid once in FY27; opening net noncurrent deficits/deposit liabilities retained at unchanged nominal amount in terminal equity. Future modeled compensation and operating expenses are treated as cash funded, so no unsupported future deficit build-up is added. This is a conditional steady-deficit convention, not a claim of immediate legal maturity. Normal opening WC liabilities are not charged twice.

valuation.model_correction_notice: Model correction — 20 October 2026: The opening-claim treatment in our earlier scenario calculations was incomplete. This revision explicitly bridges identified current settlements, retained net noncurrent claims and uncertain-composition sensitivities. The updated model replaces the earlier scenario version; the companies’ historical financial figures and published accounts have not changed.

GOV.reason: Allotment economics, related borrowing and remuneration votes are disclosed, with interested promoters excluded from special resolutions. Contrary: family-linked management, rapidly rising pay and inconsistent report headings/timing warrant controls scrutiny. No abuse established and historical margin-cash reclassification is explained.

MOAT.reason: Tested capacitor/damping products and power-quality engineering support customer qualification and technical know-how. Contrary: Shreem and major grid suppliers compete; moderate industry entry barriers and tender pricing prevent a monopoly claim.

REV.reason: Verified five-year operating-sales CAGR54.7% maps9, adjusted−1 for dependence on exceptional latest order execution and receivables. Contrary: growth before FY26 was much slower and order repeatability/customer concentration are not quantified; latest3.87×sales is not projected indefinitely.

DUR.reason: Grid integration, renewables and industrial power quality create continuing engineering needs; tested new products widen application scope. Contrary: business is project/tender sensitive, competing technology and customer spending can shift demand.

CAP.reason: Plant/testing capability and inventory conversion show productive tangible investment. Contrary: receivables and collateral tie up substantial funds, and full greenfield budget/commissioning is not verified. Fresh capital raised is not evidence of high incremental ROIC.

CASH.reason: Historical positive CFO and inventory release are counterevidence to permanent cash failure. Contrary: FY26 remains strongly negative even after separating restricted-bank movements, with₹30.31crore receivable absorption and reduced supplier funding. One weak year does not automatically trigger persistent CASH≤3 cap.

BAL.reason: ₹47.24crore equity and₹16.04crore preferential proceeds provide support; current FD offers potential project funding. Contrary:₹27.69crore debt, guarantees and pledged margins constrain flexibility, while current line headroom is unverified.

EXEC.reason: Real sales delivery, released WIP and commissioned damping-resistor supplies demonstrate execution. Contrary: collection lags, expansion timing is inconsistent and diversification ideas are not operating results.

EARN.reason: Other income₹.233crore is small; FY26 profit improvement reflects sales and operating leverage. Contrary:₹.6648crore prior-year tax, receivable quality and static depreciation during growth complicate normalized margins; cash confirmation remains weak.

R.reason: NS. The conditional funded base case gives 2.67% five-year IRR, which would map to R=1 against a 15% hurdle. This is retained as a scenario mapping only: the full project budget, usable FD release and sanctioned borrowing headroom are not verified, while the near-fourfold FY26 revenue increase lacks a customer-wise repeatability bridge. These material financing and operating assumptions are too weak for a scored expected-return input. Higher-growth scenarios are upside tests, not evidence that resolves those gaps.

D.reason: Funding/collection stress and high starting price generate substantial downside even if technical business survives. Contrary: tangible plant, operating demand and equity buffer lower immediate insolvency risk; no proven unfinanceability.

P.reason: Around41.6×static FY26 earnings after a near-fourfold sales jump demands continued strong execution. Contrary: small base and new capacity can grow, but the linked base cash/debt case does not meet15% hurdle at this quote.

L.reason: 52 observations do not establish complete60-session tradability; observed-only exit6.87days and conditional zero-gap10.34days are shown, but eight gaps and₹3.69lakh lots prevent a defensible full L score without actual calendar/no-trade verification.

gates.reason: Family management/pay risks are disclosed and voted; no established abusive transaction.
Cash-definition change substantially reconciles; incorrect chronology/loan-direction heading does not override balance-sheet scope. Exact normalized cash remains qualified, not a blanket failure.
Model exposes new borrowing needs; fresh equity and deposits provide counterevidence to automatic failure. Current sanctioned headroom unverified.
Only52 dated secondary rows in target window; coarse lots and unverified gaps meanL/IAS NS, not a fabricated no-trade count.
